question: How loud is Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green by TfL's own measurement, and what do our phone measurements add?
norm_question: how loud is liverpool street to bethnal green by tfls own measurement and what do our phone measurements add

answer.text: TfL recorded in-cab noise of 87 dB LAeq eastbound and 86 dB LAeq westbound between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, while our phone recordings add uncalibrated within-trip comparisons (a NO-GO +0.54 dB mean contrast) and indicative whole-trip saloon readings of 91.9 dB(A) and 87.3 dB(A).

verified_claims.text: In FOI-1231-2425, TfL reported measurements taken within the train operator's cab on 24 June 2024 of 87 dB LAeq eastbound from Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and 86 dB LAeq westbound from Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street.

citations.quote: these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab

verified_claims.text: A secondary press report in Brixton Buzz (27 January 2026, via JRPass) listed Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green at 92.8 decibels.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels

verified_claims.text: Our uncalibrated phone recordings average -18.66 dBFS(A) eastbound (6 runs) and -18.8 dBFS(A) westbound (5 runs) on Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green, with a NO-GO loudness verdict because the +0.54 dB mean within-trip contrast over Bethnal Green to Mile End (louder in 10 of 11 placement-ok trips) is below the 1 dB threshold, had one reversed trip (-0.13 dB on R10_WB_MLE-LST), and did not have every level variant agreeing.

Our NIOSH sound level meter app recordings in the passenger saloon add indicative whole-trip LAeq readings (including platform waits and the Bethnal Green dwell, on 1 trip per direction between Liverpool Street and Mile End) of 91.9 dB(A) eastbound and 87.3 dB(A) westbound, which may read low because the app is validated only up to about 85 dB(A) and are not like-for-like with TfL's per-section in-cab figures.
